segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Turks.
Now the cause of their setting forth was thus.
When the Turkmens were dominating over Syria, Palestine, and all the lands,
they were inflicting many evils upon the Christians who were coming to pray in Jerusalem,
especially those who were coming from Rome and the rest of the regions of Italy.
Then the Franks were stirred with zeal,
and they gathered forces and set out first for Spain,
and seized power over the cities there,
and shed much blood in them.
And they cut off the ears, noses, and lips of many foreigners {OCR? pagan/Arab?},
and put out their eyes.
Then they came against Constantinople;
and because Alexius, the king of the Greeks, would not grant them passage,
they remained warring against it for seven years.
Then they set out and came and encamped against Antioch,
and fought against it for nine months,
and were not able to capture it.
They made a secret plot with a Persian man whose name was Ruzbah,
who was guarding the tower which was on the side of that ravine called Kashkaruf,
and they promised him gold.
And over this ravine iron bars had been cast,
and upon them the tower was built.
And the Franks came by night and entered through that place,
and others ascended upon the wall with ropes.
And when they had become numerous,
they blew the horns at the last watch of the night.
And when the Turkish ruler whose name was Yaghi-Siyan woke up,
he thought that the Franks had seized the fortress,
and fear and trembling fell upon him.
And he opened the gate of the city,
and fled on the road to Aleppo with thirty men.
And when morning dawned,
he began to bite his fingers and say:
"How did I abandon the land, my family, my sons, and my wealth and possessions?" And he kept turning around, looking toward Antioch and weeping.
And from the greatness of his grief he fell from his horse;
and when those who were with him mounted him several times, and he kept falling,
they abandoned him and departed.
And a certain Armenian man came along who was cutting wood in the mountain,
and he cut off his head and carried it to the Franks.
And when the Franks had seized control of the city,
they plundered the Arabs and Turks in it,
and killed many of them.
And they made Bohemond king in it;
